mainTopic: Baking מצה on פסח: combining small batches for חלה, preventing dough from becoming חמץ, and the stages of leavening (שיאור and סידוק).
overview: The amud opens by finishing a question on רב: the גמרא explains that his 'קב' is the larger Melogna קב, which equals the חלה amount. רב יוסף reports that his household bakes מצה in small batches on פסח, and אביי objects that this stringency causes חלה to be lost. רב יוסף answers with רבי אליעזר's rule that a basket combines loaves for חלה, and the two argue over whether this applies even to separate loaves. רבי ירמיה asks whether a flat board with no rim also combines loaves, and the question ends with תיקו. A new משנה then gives three views on how three women may knead and bake מצה together without the dough becoming חמץ. A ברייתא explains the חכמים's rotation, and רבי עקיבא recalls asking רבן גמליאל about it. רבן גמליאל answered with one rule: if the dough rises, cool it with cold water. A final משנה defines the stages of rising, שיאור and סידוק. The גמרא sorts out the views of רבי יהודה and רבי מאיר, and רבא explains רבי מאיר's reason.

steps.title: The amount of flour that requires חלה
steps.stepSummary: The tail end of a question: dough of five quarters of flour and a bit more requires חלה. So how could רב recommend a smaller 'קב' batch?
steps.simpleTranslation: Dough of five quarters of flour and a little more is obligated in חלה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a challenge that began on the previous amud. It quotes the known minimum amount of dough that requires חלה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, רב said to knead a 'קב' of dough for פסח. A regular קב is only four quarters, which is less than the five quarters and a bit more needed for חלה. So it looks like רב is advising people to knead below the חלה amount.

keyTerms.meaning: The portion of dough that must be separated and given to a כהן

steps.confusionAlert: This line is not a new statement. It is the end of a question that started on the previous lines, outside this passage.

phrases.english: Five quarters of flour and a bit more
phrases.notes: The standard minimum measure for חלה

phrases.english: are obligated in challah.

steps.triggerLanguage: חמשת רבעים קמח ועוד חייבין בחלה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a challenge begun on the previous amud
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's statement recommending a 'קב' batch for פסח
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A קב seems to be less than the חלה measure, so רב appears to be advising people to avoid חלה.

steps.title: A Melogna קב equals the חלה measure
steps.stepSummary: רב meant a 'קב' of Melogna, which is a larger measure that equals exactly the חלה amount.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what רב means: a קב of Melogna is also at this very measure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by explaining which 'קב' רב meant.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The קב of the place Melogna was larger than a regular קב. It equals five quarters and a bit more. So רב was not telling people to avoid חלה at all.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what he means (re-explaining a statement)
A קב of Melogna, a larger local measure

steps.whatToRemember: רב's 'קב' for פסח is the Melogna קב, which is exactly the חלה amount. So his batch is still obligated in חלה.

phrases.english: This is what he is saying: a kav of Melogna
also stands at this measure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 1
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב meant a regular קב, which is below the חלה amount
steps.terutzMaskana: רב meant the larger Melogna קב, which equals the חלה amount

steps.title: רב יוסף's household bakes small batches on פסח
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף reports that the women of his household bake מצה in small קפיזא-sized batches on פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: Our women are accustomed to bake one קפיזא at a time for פסח.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף describes a household practice. This sets up אביי's objection in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Small batches are easier to watch so they do not become חמץ. But a קפיזא is smaller than the חלה amount. That raises the question of what happens to the חלה obligation.

keyTerms.meaning: A small measure, less than the חלה amount

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
These women of ours
are accustomed to bake kefiza by kefiza for Passover.
phrases.notes: They baked in small batches so the dough wouldn't rise and become חמץ.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר רב יוסף הני נשי דידן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new related discussion about small batches on פסח
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Baking מצה in small קפיזא batches is the practice in רב יוסף's home.

steps.title: אביי: a stringency that causes a leniency
steps.stepSummary: אביי objects: if the goal is to be strict about חמץ, this ends up being lenient, because small batches avoid חלה.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: What is your thinking, to be strict? It is a stringency that leads to a leniency, because it removes the dough from חלה.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי challenges רב יוסף's practice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being careful about חמץ is good. But making every batch smaller than the חלה amount means חלה is never taken. So one חומרא creates a קולא.

keyTerms.meaning: A stringency that leads to a leniency

steps.whyThisMatters: The idea of 'חומרא דאתי לידי קולא' is a general principle. A stringency is not acceptable if it causes another מצוה to be lost.

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
What is your reasoning, to be stringent?
It is a stringency that leads to a leniency,
since it removes it from challah.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר ליה אביי מאי דעתיך לחומרא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the practice in step 3
steps.kashyaTarget: The practice of baking small batches on פסח
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The small batches fall below the חלה amount, so the stringency about חמץ causes חלה to be lost.

steps.title: The basket combines the loaves, like רבי אליעזר
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף answers that they follow רבי אליעזר: loaves placed together in a basket combine for חלה, and שמואל rules like him.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: They act like רבי אליעזר. As it was taught, רבי אליעזר says: One who takes loaves out of the oven and puts them into a basket, the basket combines them for חלה. And רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: The הלכה is like רבי אליעזר.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף defends his household's practice by citing a ברייתא and a ruling of שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each small batch alone is too small for חלה. Once the baked מצות are put together in one basket, they count as one large amount. So חלה is taken after all, and nothing is lost.

keyTerms.meaning: One who removes bread from the oven

phrases.english: He said to him: They act in accordance with Rabbi Eliezer,
(as it was taught,) Rabbi Eliezer says:
One who removes loaves from the oven and places them in a basket,
the basket combines them for challah.
And Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
The halacha is in accordance with Rabbi Eliezer.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's objection in step 4
steps.terutzResolutionType: Citing a source that removes the problem
steps.terutzMaskana: The basket combines the batches, so חלה is still taken

steps.title: רבי יהושע בן לוי limits the basket rule
steps.stepSummary: אביי counters that רבי יהושע בן לוי limited רבי אליעזר's rule to Babylonian loaves that stick together, and not to separate stick-shaped loaves.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: But it was stated about this: רבי יהושע בן לוי said, they taught this only about Babylonian loaves that 'bite' into one another, but not about stick-shaped loaves.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי challenges רב יוסף's answer by narrowing the source he relied on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי יהושע בן לוי, the basket combines loaves only when they are stuck to each other. Separately baked loaves (כעכין) do not combine. רב יוסף's separately baked batches should therefore not combine.

keyTerms.meaning: It was stated about it (an אמורא's comment on a source)

phrases.english: He said to him: But wasn't it stated about it,
Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא כִּכָּרוֹת שֶׁל בָּבֶל
phrases.english: They taught it only regarding Babylonian loaves
that bite into one another,
but rod-like loaves, no.

steps.triggerLanguage: והא איתמר עלה אמר רבי יהושע בן לוי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the source cited in step 5
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's use of רבי אליעזר's basket rule
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The basket rule applies only to loaves stuck together, and separate small batches are not stuck together.

steps.title: רבי חנינא: even separate loaves combine
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף answers that רבי חנינא said the basket rule applies even to stick-shaped loaves, and he follows רבי חנינא.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it was stated about this: רבי חנינא said, even stick-shaped loaves.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף answers אביי by citing a different אמורא who reads the source broadly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי חנינא disagrees with רבי יהושע בן לוי. He holds that the basket combines even separate loaves. רב יוסף follows רבי חנינא, so his household's separately baked מצות do combine for חלה.
steps.whatToRemember: Baking small batches on פסח is fine as long as the מצות are gathered in a basket. According to רבי אליעזר, as explained by רבי חנינא, the basket combines even separate loaves, so חלה is not lost.

phrases.english: But wasn't it stated about it,
Rabbi Chanina said:
Even rod-like loaves.

steps.triggerLanguage: הא איתמר עלה אמר רבי חנינא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's challenge in step 6 with a competing opinion
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only loaves stuck together combine in a basket
steps.terutzMaskana: Even separate stick-shaped loaves combine, so small batches still owe חלה

steps.title: Does a flat board without a rim combine loaves?
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה asks whether a flat board with no raised edge works like a basket to combine loaves for חלה. The question turns on whether we need the inside of a vessel or only its airspace.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה asked: What is the law of a board that has no rims? Do we need the loaves to be inside a vessel? If so, that is missing here. Or perhaps we only need the airspace of a vessel, and that is present here.
steps.whatsHappening: Building on רבי אליעזר's rule that a basket combines loaves for חלה, רבי ירמיה asks about a borderline case: a flat board with no edges.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the rule depends on the loaves being physically 'inside' a container, a flat board fails, because it has no walls. If it is enough that the loaves sit in the space above a vessel, the board qualifies. The question is really about what exactly makes a basket combine the loaves.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked; introduces a genuine question (a בעיא)

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the basket rule depends on a definition. Is the key the containing walls or the shared space?

phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya asked:
A board that has no rims, what is its law?
phrases.notes: Does it combine loaves for חלה like a basket?

phrases.english: Do we require the inside of a vessel? That is missing here.
Or perhaps
We require the airspace of a vessel, and that is present here.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the accepted basket rule of רבי אליעזר (followed by רבי חנינא) and tests its boundaries with a new case.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a rimless board counts as a combining vessel: is the inside of a vessel required, or only its airspace?

steps.title: The question stays unresolved
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא ends רבי ירמיה's question with תיקו, meaning it is left unanswered.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let it stand.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes רבי ירמיה's question without deciding it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No source settles whether a rimless board combines loaves, so both sides of the question remain possible.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it stand; the question remains unresolved

phrases.english: Let it stand (unresolved).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the question raised in step 8.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Whether a rimless board combines loaves for חלה is left undecided.

steps.title: The ברייתא: basket, oven, or sticking loaves
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא records three views on what combines separate loaves for חלה. רבי אליעזר says the basket, רבי יהושע says the oven, and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says only Babylonian loaves that stick to each other.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in a ברייתא: רבי אליעזר says the basket combines the loaves. רבי יהושע says the oven combines them. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says Babylonian loaves that 'bite' into one another combine.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the original ברייתא behind the whole discussion of combining loaves for חלה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each view sets a different standard for joining small loaves into one חלה-obligated amount. For רבי אליעזר, being together in a basket is enough. For רבי יהושע, being baked together in an oven is enough. For רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, the loaves must actually be physically stuck to one another.
steps.confusionAlert: The רבי יהושע in this ברייתא is a תנא, not רבי יהושע בן לוי from step 6. רבי יהושע בן לוי limited רבי אליעזר's basket rule to loaves that stick together. In this ברייתא, it is רבן שמעון בן גמליאל who makes sticking together the standard.
steps.whatToRemember: There are three standards for combining loaves for חלה: basket (רבי אליעזר), oven (רבי יהושע), and physically stuck loaves (רבן שמעון בן גמליאל). שמואל rules like רבי אליעזר.

phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi Eliezer says:
The basket combines them.
phrases.notes: Loaves placed together in a basket combine for חלה.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua says: The oven combines them.
Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
Babylonian loaves
that bite into one another are combined.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the full ברייתא behind רבי אליעזר's basket rule, which was cited in steps 5 through 7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There is a three-way dispute on what combines loaves for חלה: basket, oven, or physical attachment.

steps.title: רבן גמליאל: knead together, bake one after another
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה begins. רבן גמליאל says three women may knead their dough at the same time and then bake in one oven, one after the other.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: רבן גמליאל says: Three women may knead at the same time and bake in one oven, one after the other.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה opens about baking מצה on פסח. רבן גמליאל gives the first view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry is that dough left waiting will become חמץ. רבן גמליאל is not concerned: even the last woman's dough, which waits while the first two bake, will not become חמץ in that time.

keyTerms.meaning: משנה; marks the start of a new משנה

phrases.english: MISHNA:
Rabban Gamliel says:
Three women may knead at the same time

phrases.aramaic: וְאוֹפוֹת בְּתַנּוּר אֶחָד, זוֹ אַחַר זוֹ.
phrases.english: and bake in one oven, one after the other.
phrases.notes: The waiting dough is not considered at risk of becoming חמץ.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה. It is related to the earlier theme of baking מצה on פסח without the dough becoming חמץ.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Three women may knead at once and bake in turn in one oven.

steps.title: חכמים: stagger the work
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים say the three women should stagger their tasks: one kneads, one arranges, and one bakes, all at the same time.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the חכמים say: Three women may be busy with dough at the same time: one kneads, one arranges, and one bakes.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים disagree with רבן גמליאל and require a staggered method, so no dough sits idle too long.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under the חכמים' method, each woman is at a different stage, so every batch keeps moving from kneading to shaping to baking without waiting. This reflects more concern than רבן גמליאל has about dough becoming חמץ while it waits.
steps.whatToRemember: רבן גמליאל allows kneading all at once and baking in turn. The חכמים require staggering so that one kneads, one shapes, and one bakes.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis say:
Three women may be engaged with dough at the same time,

phrases.aramaic: אַחַת לָשָׁה, וְאַחַת עוֹרֶכֶת, וְאַחַת אוֹפָה.
phrases.english: one kneads, one arranges, and one bakes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Presents the opposing view to רבן גמליאל in the same משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The work must be staggered: one kneads, one arranges, and one bakes at the same time.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא: No fixed schedule, just cool rising dough
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא rejects one fixed baking schedule, because women, wood, and ovens all differ. He gives one rule instead: if the dough rises, smooth it with cold water.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא says: Not all women, not all wood, and not all ovens are the same. This is the rule: if the dough starts to rise, she should smooth it with cold water.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא gives the third opinion in the משנה. He says you cannot set one timing rule for everyone. Instead, watch the dough and cool it down if it starts rising.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבן גמליאל and the חכמים both gave fixed systems for how the three women should share the oven. רבי עקיבא points out that the real speed depends on how quick the woman is, how dry the wood is, and how hot the oven is. So he switches from a set schedule to a test you can see: rising dough gets cold water.

keyTerms.meaning: It rose / swelled (the dough began to puff up)
She should smooth / pat down (the dough)

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva says:
Not all women
and not all wood
and not all ovens are the same.
This is the rule:
If it rises, she should smooth it with cold water.
phrases.notes: She wets her hands in cold water and pats the dough. This slows down the rising.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר: לֹא כׇּל הַנָּשִׁים וְלֹא כׇּל הָעֵצִים וְלֹא כׇּל הַתַּנּוּרִים שָׁוִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Third opinion in the משנה, disagreeing with the fixed systems of רבן גמליאל and the חכמים
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There is no universal timing rule. If the dough starts to rise, cool it with cold water.

steps.title: The rotation system of the three women explained
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא spells out the חכמים's rotation step by step. Each woman always keeps working with her dough, so the dough never sits idle and becomes חמץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים taught: When the first woman finishes kneading, she shapes her dough, and her friend kneads in her place. When she finishes shaping, she bakes, her friend shapes in her place, and the third woman kneads. When she finishes baking, she kneads again, her friend bakes in her place, and the third shapes. They keep going around in a circle. As long as they are working with the dough, it does not become חמץ.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that explains, step by step, how the חכמים's system from the משנה works. Each woman moves through kneading, shaping, and baking in turn.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key point is the last line: dough that is being handled does not become חמץ. The rotation is set up so that every woman's dough is always being kneaded, shaped, or baked. No dough is ever left sitting.

keyTerms.meaning: She shapes / arranges the dough into loaves
They go back around in a circle (rotate in turn)

steps.whyThisMatters: This gives the core principle behind making מצה: dough that is constantly being worked does not become חמץ.

phrases.english: GEMARA: The Rabbis taught:
Once she has kneaded, she shapes,
and her friend kneads in her place.
Once she has shaped, she bakes,
and her friend shapes in her place,
and the third woman kneads.
Once she has baked, she kneads,
and her friend bakes in her place,
and the third woman shapes,
and they go around in turn.
As long as they are busy with the dough,
it does not come to be leavened.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The גמרא explains the חכמים's rotation system from step 12
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In the rotation, each woman's dough is always being worked, and dough that is being worked does not become חמץ.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא asks רבן גמליאל which situation his rule covers
steps.stepSummary: Using a ברייתא, the גמרא returns to רבי עקיבא's words. רבי עקיבא tells how he asked רבן גמליאל whether his rule was meant for quick or slow women, wet or dry wood, and a hot or cold oven.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said, 'רבי עקיבא says: not all women...' It was taught in a ברייתא: רבי עקיבא said, I discussed this before רבן גמליאל. I asked: Let our teacher teach us, are you talking about quick women or slow women? Wet wood or dry wood? A hot oven or a cold oven?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes רבי עקיבא's words from the משנה and brings a ברייתא showing where they came from. רבי עקיבא had asked רבן גמליאל exactly which conditions his fixed rule was meant for. This step sets up רבן גמליאל's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each question matches one of רבי עקיבא's three points in the משנה: women, wood, and ovens. His argument is that a fixed timing rule only works if the conditions are known, and they always vary.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר לֹא כׇּל הַנָּשִׁים וְכוּ׳.
phrases.english: The משנה said: Rabbi Akiva says, not all women, etc.
phrases.notes: The גמרא quotes the משנה to show which words it is now discussing.

phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi Akiva said:
I discussed this before Rabban Gamliel,
Let our teacher teach us:
Is it about quick women
or about women who are not quick?
About wet wood or dry wood?
About a hot oven or a cold oven?

steps.triggerLanguage: יְלַמְּדֵינוּ רַבֵּינוּ בְּנָשִׁים זְרִיזוֹת אוֹ בְּנָשִׁים שֶׁאֵין זְרִיזוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to רבי עקיבא's statement from step 13 and shows its source
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which kind of women, wood, and oven does רבן גמליאל's fixed rule assume?

steps.title: רבן גמליאל answers: If it rises, cool it
steps.stepSummary: רבן גמליאל does not set conditions. He answers that the only rule is the one the חכמים taught: if the dough rises, smooth it with cold water.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to me: You have only what the חכמים taught. This is the rule: if the dough rises, she should smooth it with cold water.
steps.whatsHappening: רבן גמליאל answers רבי עקיבא's questions. He does not choose any one condition. He points to a simple rule that works everywhere.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of listing the right women, wood, and oven, רבן גמליאל agrees that what really counts is watching the dough. This is why רבי עקיבא's principle in the משנה uses these exact words: they came from רבן גמליאל himself, as the teaching of the חכמים.

keyTerms.meaning: You have nothing but / all you have is

steps.whatToRemember: Fixed timing systems only help in normal conditions. The rule that works everywhere is simple: if the dough begins to rise, cool it with cold water.

phrases.english: He said to me:
You have nothing but
what the Sages taught:
This is the rule:
If it rises, she should smooth it with cold water.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לִי: אֵין לְךָ אֶלָּא מַה שֶּׁשָּׁנוּ חֲכָמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי עקיבא's questions from step 15
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: No specific conditions are set. The rule that works everywhere is: if it rises, smooth it with cold water.

steps.title: New משנה: Early-stage dough is burned, but no punishment
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה rules that dough at the early stage of rising (שיאור) must be burned. Someone who eats it is exempt from punishment.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Dough at the stage of שיאור must be burned, but someone who eats it is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins about the stages of dough becoming חמץ. The first stage, שיאור, is the very beginning of rising.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שיאור dough is treated strictly enough that it must be burned, like חמץ. But it is not yet full חמץ, so someone who eats it does not get the punishment of כרת.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה (marks the start of a new משנה)
The first stage of leavening, when the dough just begins to change

steps.confusionAlert: 'Exempt' does not mean it is allowed to eat it. It must still be burned. It only means there is no כרת punishment.

phrases.english: MISHNAH: Dough at the early stage of leavening must be burned,
and one who eats it is exempt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה on a new topic: the stages of leavening
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שיאור must be burned, but eating it carries no כרת.

steps.title: Cracked dough is full חמץ with כרת
steps.stepSummary: Dough that has reached the cracking stage (סידוק) must be burned. Someone who eats it is liable to כרת, because it is full חמץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: Dough at the stage of סידוק must be burned, and someone who eats it is liable to כרת.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the second, later stage of leavening, called סידוק. At this stage the dough is full חמץ.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the contrast with the previous step. Both stages must be burned, but only סידוק dough counts as complete חמץ, so only eating it brings the punishment of כרת.

keyTerms.meaning: Cracking (the dough's surface shows cracks, meaning it is fully leavened)
Spiritual cutting off, a heavenly punishment

steps.whatToRemember: There are two stages. שיאור must be burned but brings no punishment. סידוק must be burned, and eating it brings כרת.

phrases.english: Dough at the cracking stage must be burned,
and one who eats it is liable to karet.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second half of the new משנה, contrasted with שיאור
steps.mimraCoreRuling: סידוק is full חמץ: it must be burned, and eating it brings כרת.

steps.title: רבי יהודה defines the two stages of rising
steps.stepSummary: The משנה defines שיאור as cracks like locust antennae, and סידוק as cracks that run into each other. This is רבי יהודה's view.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is שיאור? When the dough has thin cracks, like the antennae of locusts. What is סידוק? When the cracks run into one another. These are the words of רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה now explains what the two words from the earlier ruling (שיאור and סידוק) actually look like on the dough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 17 said שיאור must be burned but brings no כרת. Step 18 said סידוק brings כרת. Now רבי יהודה tells us how to tell them apart. A few thin, separate cracks are only שיאור. Cracks that cross and mix together are סידוק, which is full חמץ.

keyTerms.meaning: like the antennae of locusts, meaning thin, separate cracks
the cracks have run into and crossed each other
a crack in the surface of the dough

steps.confusionAlert: Remember these exact definitions. Later the same picture, 'like locust antennae', will mean סידוק for a different תנא, not שיאור.

phrases.english: What is siur? Like the antennae of locusts.
Cracking: when the cracks have intermingled with one another,
these are the words of Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines the two terms used in the rulings of steps 17 and 18.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For רבי יהודה, שיאור means separate thin cracks like locust antennae, and סידוק means cracks that run together.

steps.title: The חכמים say any cracking brings כרת
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים disagree. Both kinds of cracks bring כרת. For them, שיאור is only a pale surface with no cracks at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים say: whether the dough has thin cracks or crossed cracks, one who eats it is liable to כרת. So what is שיאור? Dough whose surface has turned pale, like the face of a person whose hair is standing on end from fear.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים argue with רבי יהודה. For them, once the dough has any crack at all, it is full חמץ.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the חכמים treat every crack as full חמץ, the stage with no כרת must come earlier. That earlier stage is when the dough only turns pale, with no cracks yet. So the חכמים move the word שיאור back to that pale stage.

keyTerms.meaning: this and that, meaning both kinds of cracks
whose hair stood on end, as from fright, when the face goes pale

steps.whyThisMatters: This view moves the no-כרת stage, שיאור, back to the pale-surface stage. So for the חכמים, any visible crack already makes the dough full חמץ. The גמרא will soon show that this is רבי מאיר's view.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis say:
Whether this or that, one who eats it is liable to karet.
And what is siur?
Any dough whose surface has turned pale,
like a person whose hair stands on end.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רבי יהודה's view in step 19.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Any cracking brings כרת. שיאור is only a pale surface.

steps.title: A ברייתא gives רבי מאיר's definitions
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא says רבי מאיר holds: שיאור is a pale surface, and סידוק is cracks like locust antennae.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים taught: What is שיאור? Dough whose surface turned pale, like a person whose hair stands on end. סידוק is cracks like locust antennae. These are the words of רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins by bringing a ברייתא. It shows that the 'חכמים' view in the משנה is really the view of רבי מאיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר's definitions match the חכמים of the משנה. For him, the first thin cracks already count as סידוק, meaning full חמץ.
steps.confusionAlert: Watch the switch. 'Like locust antennae' is שיאור for רבי יהודה, but it is already סידוק for רבי מאיר.

phrases.english: GEMARA: The Rabbis taught:
What is siur?
Any dough whose surface has turned pale,
like a person whose hair stands on end.
Cracking: like the antennae of locusts,
these are the words of Rabbi Meir.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Names רבי מאיר as the author of the view the משנה calls 'חכמים'.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For רבי מאיר, שיאור is a pale surface and סידוק is cracks like locust antennae.

steps.title: The ברייתא's חכמים define the stages, and both bring כרת
steps.stepSummary: In the ברייתא, the חכמים define the stages the same way רבי יהודה did. Then the ברייתא ends: both stages bring כרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים say: What is שיאור? Cracks like locust antennae. סידוק is when the cracks run together. And for both, one who eats it is liable to כרת.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives the other side, and it ends with the line 'both bring כרת'. That last line is about to cause a problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The definitions given by these חכמים are exactly רבי יהודה's definitions from the משנה. But the closing line seems to say that even שיאור brings כרת. That does not fit what רבי יהודה says in the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: liable to the punishment of כרת, being cut off

phrases.english: And the Rabbis say:
What is siur? Like the antennae of locusts.
Cracking: when the cracks have intermingled with one another.
And whether this or that, one who eats it is liable to karet.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא with the other opinion and the closing line about כרת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ברייתא's חכמים use רבי יהודה's definitions, and the text then says both stages bring כרת.

steps.title: Challenge: the משנה says שיאור brings no כרת
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: our משנה says שיאור brings no כרת according to רבי יהודה. So how can the ברייתא say both stages bring כרת?
steps.simpleTranslation: But we learned in the משנה: שיאור must be burned, and one who eats it is exempt. These are the words of רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ending of the ברייתא by quoting the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא's חכמים hold the same definitions as רבי יהודה, so they seem to be the same view. Yet the משנה says that for רבי יהודה, eating שיאור brings no כרת. So the line 'both bring כרת' cannot belong to this view.

keyTerms.meaning: but did we not learn in a משנה? This opens a challenge.

phrases.english: But didn't we learn in the mishna:
Siur must be burned, and one who eats it is exempt,
these are the words of Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the closing line of the ברייתא in step 22.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's line 'זה וזה האוכלו חייב כרת' placed under the חכמים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Those חכמים hold רבי יהודה's definitions, and the משנה says רבי יהודה exempts someone who eats שיאור from כרת.

steps.title: Answer: the karet line belongs to רבי מאיר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers: read the ending as רבי מאיר's view. For רבי מאיר, both kinds of cracks bring כרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say it this way: according to רבי מאיר, for both this and that, one who eats it is liable to כרת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the reading of the ברייתא. The last line goes back to רבי מאיר, not to the חכמים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי מאיר, any crack at all is already סידוק, so both crack stages bring כרת. The ברייתא's חכמים, like רבי יהודה, still say that early thin cracks bring no כרת. Now the ברייתא and the משנה fit together.

keyTerms.meaning: say it this way; it introduces a corrected reading

steps.whatToRemember: There are two views. רבי יהודה (and the ברייתא's חכמים): thin cracks are שיאור with no כרת, and crossed cracks are סידוק with כרת. רבי מאיר (the משנה's חכמים): any crack brings כרת, and שיאור is only a pale surface.

phrases.english: Say:

phrases.aramaic: לְרַבִּי מֵאִיר, זֶה וָזֶה הָאוֹכְלוֹ חַיָּיב כָּרֵת.
phrases.english: According to Rabbi Meir, whether this or that, one who eats it is liable to karet.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 23.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reassigning a line of the ברייתא to a different speaker
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא's חכמים said that both crack stages bring כרת.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only רבי מאיר says that both crack stages bring כרת. The ברייתא's חכמים agree with רבי יהודה.

steps.title: רבא explains רבי מאיר's reason
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that every crack on top has many cracks hidden below it. So even one small crack shows the dough is full חמץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: What is רבי מאיר's reason? Every single crack you see on top has several more cracks underneath it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא explains why רבי מאיר treats even the first thin cracks as full חמץ.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The surface shows less than what is going on inside the dough. One crack on top means the inside has already cracked a lot. So the dough has really reached the crossed-cracks stage on the inside.
steps.whyThisMatters: This gives a logical basis for the stricter view. A small sign on the surface can show a bigger change hidden inside.

phrases.english: Rava said:
What is the reason of Rabbi Meir?

phrases.aramaic: אֵין לָךְ כׇּל סֶדֶק וָסֶדֶק מִלְּמַעְלָה
phrases.english: You have no crack at all on top
that does not have several cracks below it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reasoning behind רבי מאיר's view, which was just confirmed in step 24.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A crack on the surface shows many cracks inside, so any crack means full חמץ.
